🇺🇸🇮🇷 Trump can't win the Iran war, but the Democrats may help him keep fighting it

Drop Site News co-founder Ryan Grim believes Trump has trapped himself in a devastating political and military dead end.

He can't achieve the victory he wants, but walking away would mean admitting defeat.

Ryan believes that America lacks the military resources needed to fundamentally change the conflict, while Iran has every incentive to keep raising the cost of Washington's economic pressure.

And the longer the confrontation drags on, the harder it becomes to end, because Iran has already suffered too much to accept a return to the same sanctions that existed before the war.

But there's another danger emerging in Washington.

Democrats campaigned on ending the conflict, yet with war funding approaching a critical deadline, he warns that hawkish Democrats could join Republicans to keep the money flowing.

And Democratic leadership is already showing troubling signs of reluctance to confront U.S military support for Israel.

Even Hakeem Jeffries refused to commit to bringing legislation restricting some weapons transfers to Israel to a vote.

Ryan believes Trump has a rare opportunity to declare victory, end the confrontation and turn his attention to America's economy.

But he doubts he will take it.

And if Washington refuses to change course, the Iran war could become exactly what Trump once promised America would never fight again: another endless Middle Eastern conflict.

AI used 17 million lines of code to prove the Riemann Hypothesis. 

That’s extraordinary. 

But perhaps the deeper wonder is Riemann himself.  In 1859, with nothing but a human mind, he glimpsed a hidden order: primes appear random, yet every nontrivial zero of the zeta function lies on one line, that is Re(s) = 1/2.  

Since then, human mathematicians have checked millions of zeros. Not one has broken the pattern.  

The line may be the creator’s grace, but seeing it was humanity’s triumph.  

Machines can prove. But the imagination that finds order in chaos, and reaches toward the edge of the universe, still belongs to humans.

Governor of Russia's Murmansk region, Andrey Chibis, has been arrested.

He is suspected of involvement in the theft of over 39 million rubles from the regional Ministry of Construction’s budget, as well as the misappropriation of 1 billion rubles allocated for road reconstruction, and engaging in illegal foreign currency transactions.

He's the first acting Russian governor to be arrested after the start of Russia's full-scale war against Ukraine.

Comment from me:
Russia's war has brought mounting fiscal strain on Murmansk region. Regional public debt reached 78.1 billion rubles (almost $1 billion)  as of September 1, 2026.

The EU added the Port of Murmansk and associated Arctic shipping/oil transport entities to its sanctions list in April 2026 (under its 20th sanctions package), followed by additional vessel and fuel-supply listings in June 2026 affecting vessels operating around Kola Bay and the Barents Sea. Earlier US sanctions also targeted the Lavna coal terminal project in Murmansk.

Russia is rerouting its logistical corridors in the area towards China but sanctions make it more complicated.

A lot of Murmansk's Nortern Fleet and other personnel from its naval, marine and air/air defense units have been sent to the front lines. Confirmed losses include soldiers, marines and senior officers.

Putin's war of aggression is putting an increasingly greater toll on Russia's regional economies. We are likely to see more cases like Chibis's one as Russia grows poorer.

Markets rally before Jensen's return is announced, raising questions about whether it was insider information or a relief bounce

"Donald Trump doubled down on the pressure just, I believe, yesterday, saying that the Nvidia board should reinstate him. As of this morning, it happened."

"Nvidia was up 30% just pre-market, from the 130s up into the 160s on this news. The Nasdaq was up 6, 7, 8% pre-market on this news."

"Markets were already bouncing before this Nvidia news was announced. You have to draw a couple of conclusions."

"If you're cynical and you believe in conspiracy theories, I don't really know if I do or not. This was insider information. People knew that he was coming back."

"The second argument is that this was just an overblown bearish excitement and euphoria. And after that kind of volatility, you get a major bounce."

"Absolutely astounding. Jensen Huang is back as the CEO of Nvidia."

Nvidia short sellers are set to take about $12.2 billion in paper losses today as shares jump to $168.50 on Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as CEO.

That would be their biggest one-day loss since at least 2019.

The reversal is sharp. Short sellers had made about $24 billion in paper gains as Nvidia fell 35% from its Oct. 6 all-time high through Nov. 16, per S3 Partners. The selloff gave Nvidia its worst week since the April 2025 tariff shock.
